text: On Monday I began a careful inventory of the objects stored in the little workshop behind our house. Each shelf had a paper label, but several labels had faded until the writing was difficult to read. I carried a lamp from the kitchen and placed it beside the doorway where the extension cable could reach. The first box contained wooden handles, bent nails, and three hinges wrapped in a piece of newspaper. I counted every item before moving the box onto a clean section of the workbench near the window. My brother arrived after breakfast with a notebook that still had plenty of blank pages at the back. He wrote down the measurements while I held each object against the ruler and checked the markings twice. Outside the window a delivery driver stopped briefly to ask which house had ordered a new garden hose. We pointed him toward our neighbor and returned to the shelf where the larger tools were kept. The old saw had a cracked handle, so we set it aside and marked it for repair before summer. Under the saw we discovered a packet of photographs showing the same workshop before any shelves were installed. One picture showed our grandfather painting the window frame while a ladder rested against the unfinished wall. Another showed a much younger version of our mother holding a basket filled with apples from the yard. We placed those photographs in a dry envelope rather than leaving them underneath the heavy metal tools. By lunchtime the workbench had become a neat arrangement of small piles, each accompanied by a handwritten description. I opened the door to let fresh air move through the room while we ate sandwiches on the steps. After lunch we checked the inventory against the shelves again and corrected two entries that listed the wrong size. The afternoon light made the room easier to inspect, especially the dark corner behind the stack of empty crates. We swept that corner carefully and found a brass button that must have fallen from an old work coat. Before closing the final box, we compared its contents with a list that had been pinned behind the door. Several entries used different names for the same tools, so we added a short explanation beside each uncertain description. I checked the remaining drawers carefully and wrote down the location of every spare handle, screw, washer, and wooden peg. At the very end of the notebook I added a note describing an amber lantern stored above the doorway. That final note matters because the description appears beyond the portion of text used by the scoring models. We locked the workshop before dinner and left the finished inventory on the kitchen table for everyone to read.
